channel.title: Pass Your Electrician Exam Blog
channel.description: Electrician exam prep study tips, NEC changes and licensing news.

item.title: Best Way to Study for Master Electrician Exam: Proven Tips 2026
item.description: Passing the master electrician exam requires more than just raw knowledge; it demands strategic study and smart preparation. The foundation of your success is the 2026 National Electrical Code (NEC), which is the official reference during the open-book exam. Instead of trying to memorize vas

item.title: What to Expect on Electrician Exam Day, From Check-In to Your Score
item.description: A walk through the day itself: what to bring, what the check-in looks like, how the testing room works, how to pace the clock, and what happens to your result afterwards.

item.title: How to Study for the Journeyman Electrician Exam: A 6-Week Plan
item.description: Most people fail the journeyman exam on time, not knowledge. Here is a six-week plan that trains you to find answers in the code book fast, with a calculations block every week.

item.title: How the Journeyman Electrician Exam Is Structured
item.description: Question counts, time limits, the content outline, how the pass mark works, and which code articles carry most of the weight on a typical state journeyman exam.

item.title: Journeyman vs Master Electrician Exam: What Actually Changes
item.description: The master exam is not the journeyman exam with harder questions. It adds services, load calculations, transformers, design and supervision, and in many states a business and law section.

item.title: Open-Book Exam: How to Use the Code Book Under a Clock
item.description: Open book is where most candidates lose. A method for deciding what to look up, how to get to the right section in seconds, and how to read an exception without missing the condition.

item.title: How to Tab Your NEC for the Electrician Exam
item.description: Which articles and tables deserve a tab, how to place them so they stay useful, what the testing centres allow, and why doing it yourself is part of the study.

item.title: The NEC Articles That Carry Most of the Exam Questions
item.description: Twelve articles and a handful of tables account for most of the questions on journeyman and master exams. What each one covers, what gets asked, and the sections to know cold.

item.title: The Calculations You Must Be Able to Do Before Exam Day
item.description: A checklist of the eight calculation families on journeyman and master exams, what each one needs from the code book, and the mistake that costs the most points in each.

item.title: Voltage Drop on the Electrician Exam: Formula, Traps and a Worked Example
item.description: The two voltage-drop formulas, where the constants come from, the 3 and 5 percent recommendations, and a worked example that shows why the obvious conductor is often one size too small.

item.title: Box Fill and Conduit Fill, Step by Step
item.description: The two fill calculations on every exam, worked from the tables that govern them: how to count conductors in a box under 314.16, and how to size a raceway with Chapter 9 Tables 1, 4 and 5.

item.title: Motor Circuits on the Exam: Why Candidates Miss Them
item.description: Motor questions use table currents for some things and nameplate currents for others, and the percentages change by device. The four-step method, a worked example and the traps.

item.title: Dwelling Load Calculations: Standard Method vs Optional Method
item.description: The two ways to size a dwelling service under Article 220, worked side by side on the same house, with the demand factors each one uses and the places the exam checks whether you mixed them up.

item.title: How to Use Practice Exams: The Error Log Method
item.description: Practice exams are not for finding out whether you would pass. They are for finding the code sections you keep missing. A method for taking them, logging misses by section, and turning the log into the last two weeks of study.

item.title: Failed the Electrician Exam? What to Change for the Retake
item.description: How to read the score report, why most second attempts fail for the same reason as the first, and a four-week plan that changes the thing that actually went wrong.

item.title: From Apprentice to Journeyman: Documenting Your Hours and Applying to Test
item.description: What counts toward the experience requirement, how to prove it, what the application usually asks for, and how long the approval takes so you can study while the paperwork moves.

item.title: Moving Your Electrician License to Another State: How Reciprocity Works
item.description: What reciprocity actually means, the conditions nearly every agreement attaches, what happens when there is no agreement, and how to avoid the mistakes that turn a transfer into a full reapplication.

item.title: Pacing and Nerves: Managing the Clock on Exam Day
item.description: A time budget for a 100-question exam, the three-pass method, what to do when a question will not come, and the small physical habits that keep your head clear for four hours.
